title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

errors: No genuine mathematical error. Points to note:
(vi)(b) as written ('or the reverse') is only T0 separation, so the points are determined only up to the Kolmogorov quotient. Grothendieck acknowledges this in NB1.

The reductions in NB2 ((iii) ⇔ (iii') + Ax L2; (ii) ⇔ Ax L3 + (iii'); (iv) follows from the others) depend on the exact form of Ax L1–L3, which are not on this page. They are plausible but cannot be checked here.
In (ii), X∩Y must mean a combinatorially defined set of common pieces (after common subdivision), not a set-theoretic intersection. Otherwise the formula is circular.

ideas.what: Realization of an abstract part/overlap/disjointness structure by a 'support' map into the subsets of a point set. The map is required to be monotone, to send disjointness exactly to empty intersection, and to send combinatorial intersection to set intersection.
ideas.modern_name: Point-set representation of a mereological / mereotopological structure; representation theorem for region-based theories of space (cf. Stone representation of lattices as fields of sets; representation of contact algebras)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead, de Laguna, Tarski (region-based geometry); Stone (1936); modern contact-algebra representations by Düntsch–Winter, Dimov–Vakarelov (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of tame topology in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this axiomatization appears unpublished

ideas.what: Normalizing a realization by passing to the quotient of points with the same set of containing supports.
Reducing the realization to its values on elementary pieces L, with the axioms on general objects becoming the L-axioms plus a single disjointness condition (iii').
ideas.modern_name: Determining a lattice morphism by its values on join-generators / atoms

ideas.what: The question (prepared here, posed on p.74) whether the support data determine the point set P up to unique isomorphism, via an ordered set ΣM of abstract supports.
ideas.modern_name: Reconstruction of points from a frame or region algebra (sober spaces, Stone/locale duality, points as ultrafilters or clusters in mereotopology)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 combinatorial Analysis situs, as axiomatized here, is a region-based ('point-free') theory of space. Points are an optional extra structure given by a support map. Its axioms closely parallel those of mereotopology and contact algebras: part-of, overlap and disjointness, with a representation by point sets plus a T0 normalization. The literature on Grothendieck's tame topology does not seem to connect it with this tradition, and the mereotopology literature does not cite this.
missed.quote: X || Y ⟺ |X| ∩ |Y| = ∅ ... la force de l'axiome dans l'implication ⇐
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests reading Grothendieck's 'géométrie modérée' notes as a representation-theorem programme. One would ask which combinatorial structures M admit a unique point realization. That question has precise analogues in mereotopology (and o-minimal/PL settings) that could be compared or transferred.

missed.claim: The uniqueness question for the point realization of a combinatorial structure (canonical iso ΣM ≅ supports in P(P)) is set up here and posed on p.74, apparently without resolution.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete, checkable reconstruction problem for his axioms Ax L1–L3. It is only modestly novel given known Stone-type dualities.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful, unpublished axiomatization of 'realizations by points' of a combinatorial space structure. It is essentially a point-free/mereotopological representation set-up with a Kolmogorov normalization. The individual ideas are standard, but the framing as part of Grothendieck's tame-topology programme, and the implicit link to region-based geometry, appear undocumented.
transcription_corrections: Margin: 'la force de l'axiome est dans l'implication ⇐'.
NB1 likely reads 'L'axiome (vi) est dans la nature d'une normalisation ; il suffit de remplacer P par son quotient par la relation d'équivalence...'.

NB2: 'Mais la validité des conditions (i) à (iv) équivaut à des conditions sur |Z|' (approximate). Then: 'La condition (iii) p.ex. équivaut à la condition (iii') pour x, y ∈ L, + la condition Ax L2. La condition (ii) équivaut à Ax L3 et (iii').'
Last line: 'Donc, la variante [revient à se donner une application] L → P(P), x ⟼ |x|' satisfying the conditions continued on p.74. 'Je suppose [satisfaites] les conditions' refers to Ax L.
The relation symbol in (ii) is written as a struck-through order or comparison sign (compatibility/non-transversality), not clearly ⊥.
In (vi), the sub-labels (a) covering and (b) separation were inserted, with (a) logically preceding (b).
